leak_test_details: Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/83a4d5f8-8137-5cb1-9baa-8ac55fed2a66/scratchpad/ml/verify_tune/leak.js (outputs in leak_2022-23.out, leak_2023-24.out, leak_2024-25.out in the same folder). It covered 3 seasons (2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25) and rounds 5, 12, 20 and 33 of each, so 12 cases. For each case I built a truncated copy of the season. All hist rows with round >= r were removed. Fixtures of round >= r were set unfinished with null scores. Events >= r were set fin=false, round r was made nxt, and avg was nulled. Every numeric player column after the first 8 was nulled, keeping code. I checked that no hist row with round >= r was left. btRound only adds a player as a target if he has a round-r history row, so I added a stats-free stub row for round r. The stub carries only the fixture facts known before the round: r, opp, home flag, fixture id, and pts=0 as a placeholder that has no effect on pred. Path A ran the model's own btRound(r) on the truncated data. Path B was the production path: pmPredictAll on live-like truncated data, with season-to-date totals rebuilt from the truncated history through BT_MAP, every player available, and the club taken from btTeamAt on the stub. Both were compared with the full-data btRun predictions for round r. Result: in all 12 cases both paths gave the same player set (no player missing or extra) and a max absolute difference of exactly 0. Between 363 and 429 players per round. A first version of path B differed by up to 0.19 in some January-window rounds. The cause was my harness: it left non-predicted target players at their end-of-season club. Once every round-r player was assigned his round-r club with btTeamAt, as btRound does, the difference was 0 everywhere. So that mismatch came from my construction, not from the experiment.
other_leakage_or_protocol_issues: No leakage found. Compared with fp_model.js, the diff only touches the PM constants: K_FIN goes from 3 to 1e6, and a new SH map (card=1e6, others null) plus K_FIN_A=null are added. It also touches the shr/fin helpers and the rate keys in pmPlayer, plus one method-text line. These rates read p.expected_goals and similar fields and the position priors C.pri. In the replay both are rebuilt from rows with round < r (btRound uses BT_MAP sums over earlier rows, and pmCtx priors use the rebuilt d.P). The change does not use end-of-season totals, final prices, xP, same-round data or 2025-26. It has no learned model and no previous-season priors. model_tunable.js with its defaults is the same as v1. search.js, conservative.js, paired.js and check.js load only 2022-23 and 2023-24, and only final.js touches 2024-25. I re-ran conservative.js and paired.js in my folder on TRAIN only and got the claimed numbers. Conservative 1.72407, made of 1.68787 and 1.76027. Full optimum 1.72259. Conservative vs baseline: +0.00643 +- 0.00128 per gameweek, 50/69 wins. Full vs conservative: +0.00154 +- 0.00097, 39/69 wins. Small points: SH.card=1e6 is outside the search grid (max 12000). It was picked after the search, on TRAIN only (1.72407 vs 1.72418 for card=12000), so it is a negligible post-hoc choice and not a VALIDATION choice. Two VALIDATION looks are declared (the original plus an identical re-run). I cannot independently verify when the earlier look happened. No file shows VALIDATION being used for selection. There is also an earlier TRAIN-only search variant (search_v2_missas0.out). Club assignment in btRound uses the round-r row's opponent and home flag (btTeamAt). This was already in v1, is not introduced by this change, and uses only information known from the fixture list.
